road.title: Where you are from
road.description: Someone of no particular height, which they regard as a professional asset in a coat with more pockets than the law requires, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Leopold is a Border Official and administers a border that moved away one night and stamps papers so that it will know where to come back to.

openObjectives.prompt: Leopold has a form with a space marked ORIGIN and intends to fill it. Tell Leopold where you are from, using Italian.
Tell Leopold where you live, using Italian.
Leopold has noticed your accent and is being polite about it, with visible effort. Tell Leopold that you speak a little of their language, using Italian.

character.name: Leopold Nettlebed
character.description: Someone of no particular height, which they regard as a professional asset in a coat with more pockets than the law requires, leaning on a staff with notches cut for every complaint. Leopold is a Border Official and administers a border that moved away one night and stamps papers so that it will know where to come back to.

npc.narrative: You find Leopold in the bosco, smiling with great effort, like a man holding a door shut. A piccolo stamp sits on a stump beside him, worn at the handle and recently apologised to. It is mezzogiorno and the sky is clear.
npc.native: Buongiorno! Sono di qui, but my border is not. Abito in this hut and parlo with my stamp, Gerald. Now tell me, please: where are you from, where do you live, and what do you speak?

player: Sono di Austria e abito a Copenaghen.

correction.text: Sono dell'Austria e abito a Copenaghen.
correction.translation: I am from Austria and I live in Copenhagen.

verdict.overallFeedback: You told Leopold where you are from and where you live, and your sentence was nearly perfect. Just mind the article before a country name, and next time tell him about the language too.

objectiveResults.feedback: Good try with "sono di"! With a country name you need the article: "Sono dell'Austria" (or "Sono di Vienna" with a city).
Well done, "abito a Copenaghen" is exactly right for telling where you live.
You haven't said yet that you speak a little of Leopold's language, so Leopold will ask you about it again later.

correction.text: Sono dell'Austria e abito a Copenaghen.
correction.translation: I am from Austria and I live in Copenhagen.

openObjectives.prompt: Leopold has noticed your accent and is being polite about it, with visible effort. Tell Leopold that you speak a little of their language, using Italian.

npc.narrative: The midday sole lies flat across the counter, where Leopold Nettlebed is smiling at a ledger with visible effort. Gerald sits on his blotter, worn down on one side from a drop nobody mentions. Through the finestra there is a campo, and in it a pale rectangle where something used to stand.
npc.native: Austria e Copenaghen: molto lontano. Gerald is checking his ink for such distances. In Copenaghen, what language do you speak?

player: Parlo inglese e un po' di danese. E parlo un po' di italiano!

verdict.overallFeedback: Well done! You said which languages you speak and added that you speak a little Italian, all in good Italian.

objectiveResults.feedback: You told Leopold you speak a little Italian with "parlo", used correctly.

vocabularyEvidence.evidence: E parlo un po' di italiano!

npc.narrative: The porta of the hut stands open to the sole. Gerald comes down on your carta once, piano, as if apologising to it, and the little finestra seems to nod. Leopold smiles, under protest, with all his denti.
npc.native: Inglese, danese e un po' di italiano! Gerald is impressed, and he is hard to impress, being a stamp. Safe travels back to Copenaghen, and my regards to Austria. Buon viaggio e arrivederci!
npc.translation: English, Danish and a little Italian! Gerald is impressed, and he is hard to impress, being a stamp. Safe travels back to Copenhagen, and my regards to Austria. Have a good trip and goodbye!

player: Grazie! Copenaghen è bella ma fredda.

npc.narrative: The sole stands directly over the capanna, and Gerald sits open on the desk, drying in it. Leopold leans across the finestra and lowers his voice, though the only listener is a cane asleep in the erba.
npc.native: Bella ma fredda! Between us, my dog walks in the grass at dusk, never on the road. Copenaghen è grande?
npc.translation: Beautiful but cold! Between us, my dog walks in the grass at dusk, never on the road. Is Copenhagen big?

player: Sì, è grande. Ma perché il cane non cammina sulla strada?

npc.narrative: Leopold leans out of the capanna and looks at the strada as if it might overhear. Out in the erba, a cane lies very still, pretending to be a hedge. Gerald, the timbro, is apologised to for no reason, and lowers his voce.
npc.native: Il cane non cammina sulla strada.
npc.translation: The dog does not walk on the road. At dusk he sits, stares at nothing, then goes into the grass. I think he is being polite. Do you have a dog in Copenhagen?
